text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- The current EU dispute with the United States over the Helms-Burton legislation threatening sanctions on non-U.S. companies trading with communist Cuba is succeeding in forcing Danish companies to stay away from an upcoming trade fair on the island. Only four Danish companies in all are to participate in the 1996 Havana International Fair next week.

--- Danish State Railways (DSB) and Denmark's largest electricity company Nesa are to compete against leading telecommunications group Tele Danmark by granting foreign telecom operators access to their fibre-optic cables, creating an alternative telephone network.

--- Information technology firm Maersk Data, part of shipping group A.P. Moeller, is to open a new subsidiary in Madras, India in December as joint venture with India's Thapar Group's Crompton Greaves.

--- Western Danish Vestas windmill factory is to deliver two big wind energy parks to China and Ireland worth in toto 240 million crowns. The orders are for twenty-five 600 kilowatt windmills for Scottish Power Plc in Ireland and 56 mills for China's Xinjiang Electric Power Co.
--- Leading Danish industrial shareholders are now the third most-heavily taxed in the European Union with total taxes at 60.4 percent of share profits, according to a new European survey.
